In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the baryon current effects are small and that the dominant effect is the inclusion of the b K − N amplitude.
the impulse approximation is in reasonable agreement with the data.
the baryon recoil effects are not large, but not small either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of the b K − N → K − Λ amplitude is essential for the correct description of strangeness changing reactions, but the explicit inclusion of the b N momentum is not.
we have shown that the momentum dependence of the K − N → t Λπ amplitude is very important for the calculation of the (K −,π − ) reaction, and that the momentum dependence is not well understood.
the momentum operator is a very important ingredient in the description of resonance production in strangeness changing nuclear interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the momentum dependence of the t K − N amplitude should be included in any realistic calculations of strangeness changing nuclear processes.
the baryon recoil effect in the input amplitude is essential for the correct description of (K −, π−) reactions.
the momentum dependence in the t K − N amplitude is essential to achieve agreement with experiment.
